title: [Hebrew: Sefer pardes rimmonim]
shelf_note: Cordovero's Pardes Rimmonim, a core work of Safed Kabbalah; the scans are of that work (Gate 6 'Seder Amidatan', Gate 23 'Erkhei ha-Kinuyim', Gate 31 'Sha'ar ha-Neshamah').
structure_note: Two record populations in one book: negative page numbers (-135, -32) are unsplit two-page openings (image names 0135-full.jpg, 0032-full.jpg) and positive numbers are split single pages (sp….jpg). page_records 521 against pages_count 348 and 40 printed numbers with 20 backsteps fit openings and split leaves being interleaved, so a reader probably meets the same text twice and in a broken order. Page numbers below 1 are a structural defect in themselves.
reader_summary: This is Cordovero's Pardes Rimmonim, and the headwords and running heads are mostly the right ones. The body of the transcription is not the printed text. The rabbinic (Rashi) type is read as streams of ס/ק-substituted nonsense, and the English turns that into fluent invented Kabbalah: angels named 'Mardiel' and 'Zevachiel', 'the numerical value is 15'. None of the English can be trusted.

title: שיר השירים (Shīr ha-Shīrīm / Song of Songs)
shelf_note: A Yemenite-type manuscript of the Song of Songs: the Hebrew verse, the Aramaic Targum, and Judeo-Arabic (tafsir) lines, with Masoretic notes at the foot of the page. It belongs on a Hebrew shelf; the Folkscanomy 'religion_bible' collection is a generic home for it.
structure_note: 33 records, all transcribed and translated. The catalogue gives 'published 1500' and author 'Solomon', but this is a manuscript, not a printed edition of 1500 (catalogue format wrong, I7). The 2 backsteps likely come from mixed numbering: the OCR takes a later pencil folio ('179') and turns it into a Hebrew header 'קעט'.
reader_summary: This is the Targum to the Song of Songs, interleaved verse by verse with the Hebrew text, in a Yemenite-type manuscript. The Hebrew and Aramaic transcription is largely right, and the English follows the Targum well. Two things go wrong. On some pages the two columns are put in the wrong order. And the Judeo-Arabic lines are not recognised as Arabic, so they are rendered as garbled Aramaic or misread outright: Elijah becomes 'the Lord', and 'I said I will climb the palm' becomes 'your fingers'.

title: Shulhan Arukh, Hoshen ha-Mishpat
shelf_note: Karo's Shulhan Arukh, Hoshen Mishpat, with a commentary ('פירוש') in the outer column; it fits a Hebrew shelf.
structure_note: Date 1565 is doubtful: these pages carry a printed marginal commentary and handwritten Arabic page numbers (33, 62), which look like a later edition rather than the Venice 1565 first edition (low confidence). The 33 backsteps are probably misread Hebrew numerals plus the handwritten Arabic numbers, not a scan splice. 30 pages lack OCR.
reader_summary: This is Hoshen Mishpat with a marginal commentary, and the siman headings are the right text. The transcription of the main text is full of letter confusions (ס for ש, ח for א, 'נלחמות' for נאמנות), and the commentary in Rashi type is mostly lost. The English reconstructs the sense in places but twice reverses the ruling: 98:1 says one does not presume a waiver, and 341:1 says the lender may reclaim an unspecified loan at will. Siman numbers are also shifted (97–98 is rendered as 107–108). A halakhist could not rely on it.

title: Jesuitici templi stupenda
shelf_note: The scans are Hayyim Vital's Etz Hayyim (Lurianic Kabbalah): the running heads read 'היכל א … שער מטי ולא מטי', there is a 'הקדמת עץ החיים' and the colophon says 'תם ונשלם ספר הקדוש עץ חיים'. The content belongs on a Kabbalah shelf, but the record calls it 'Jesuitici templi stupenda' by Joachim Beringer (1610), a Latin anti-Jesuit tract. The catalogue identity is wrong.
structure_note: Catalogue identity wrong (I7: title, author and date belong to another work). Three of four sampled records have negative page numbers (-64, -19, -4) and are unsplit two-page openings, beside split positive pages (206). page_records 311 against pages_count 208 suggests openings and split leaves are mixed, as in slot 17. Only 20 of 208 counted pages are translated.
reader_summary: The scans are Etz Hayyim, catalogued under the wrong title as a Latin Jesuit pamphlet. No sampled page has a real transcription. Two are invented text: modern Hebrew prose about Temple gates, and a generic sermon on 'mati ve-lo mati'. The other two are letter-substituted garbage, and one of those repeats a line ten times. The English translates all of it as if it were the book.
